# ADR-012: Mobile Companion Communication & Pairing

**Status:** ACCEPTED | **Date:** 2026-09-22 | **Owners:** Mobile/Realtime Communication Architect

## Context
Mobile app must securely pair with a specific browser session and relay voice/commands
(Section 3.10).

## Decision
**Pairing**: QR code or short-lived numeric code generated by the browser extension, encoding an
ephemeral pairing token (single-use, short TTL, e.g. 2 minutes) exchanged through the Mobile
Pairing Service (backend), never peer-to-peer without backend mediation, to allow revocation and
audit.

**Session channel**: WebSocket to the Session Gateway (backend-relayed) as the baseline for
universal NAT traversal and simplicity; WebRTC data channel considered as a **future
optimization** for lower-latency push-to-talk audio once the baseline is proven — not required
for v1 (avoids the complexity of STUN/TURN infrastructure in the first vertical slice).

```
Browser Extension --QR/code--> Mobile App --ephemeral token--> Session Gateway <--WebSocket--> Browser Extension
```

## Threat model (subsystem-specific)
- **Token replay**: single-use tokens, invalidated immediately on first successful pairing.
- **Session hijack**: session bound to a signed, short-TTL session credential rotated
  periodically; Gateway validates origin/device fingerprint drift and can force re-pairing.
- **Confused deputy**: mobile app never receives raw page content or unrestricted browser
  control — it sends `UserIntent`-shaped commands through the same contract as voice, subject to
  the same capability-class confirmation policy (ADR-014); it cannot invoke skills directly.
- **Eavesdropping**: channel encrypted end-to-end at the transport layer (TLS/WSS); payload-level
  encryption considered for defense-in-depth (NEEDS VERIFICATION — cost/benefit vs. TLS-only,
  pending threat model review in ADR-014).

## Failure modes
Pairing service unavailable → mobile app cannot pair (clear error), but does not affect
browser-only operation (ADR-016 principle: subsystem failure isolation).

## Consequences
WebSocket relay adds one hop of latency vs. WebRTC; accepted for v1 simplicity, revisited once
push-to-talk latency is measured against user expectations.

## Revisit triggers
Push-to-talk latency in the vertical slice exceeding target NFRs (see `07-testing-strategy.md`
adjacent NFR doc).

## References
